_note: The words that make GilbertOne show the ambulance numbers instead of answering. Read by apps/web/src/lib/assistant.ts, generated into Swift and Kotlin by scripts/emit-assistant.mjs, and checked by scripts/check-boundaries.mjs. The matching rules — stems, gaps, folded diacritics, reading everything — are in packages/catalog/assistant.json; this file is only the list, and the record of every change to it.
_whyItsOwnFile: The founder decided on 14 September 2026 that the list is to be proposed and then configured as MyThuso goes. A list that changes on that rhythm, and that a clinician will one day review line by line, reads better in a file that holds nothing else: a change to a term is a change to this file, with its own version and changelog entry, and never a change to GilbertOne's contract. The rules that decide how a term is matched stay with GilbertOne, because changing those is a change to how GilbertOne reads, not to what it listens for.

acceptedBy.decision: Propose it; we can configure as we go.

use: These words only ever raise. A match turns the answer into the emergency answer; the absence of a match lowers nothing, decides nothing and is never shown as reassurance. False positives are acceptable — somebody asking about a stroke they had years ago is shown the ambulance numbers — and a miss is not made safe by GilbertOne being silent about it, which is why the sentence under silenceIsNotSafety stays on the screen beside every conversation.

changelog.by: Engineering (the Gilbert and Voice build), accepted by the Founder
changelog.why: The proposed starting list: drafted from the eight conditions in packages/catalog/sos.json, a crisis group and a general group, and widened the same day after the Wave 1 review found word forms it missed. Not reviewed by a clinician.

howToChange: Edit the words under `groups`. Words are lower-case letters and digits with single spaces, and a word belongs to one group only.
Raise `version` by one and add a changelog entry with the same version, the day, who made the change by role, every term added and every term removed as "group: term", and why.
Put the entry's termsHash in: node scripts/check-boundaries.mjs prints the hash the new list has when it does not match.

The shared fixtures in packages/catalog/assistant.json must still pass on the web, iOS and Android, so a change cannot silence a listed emergency. The falsePositives below are reported and never block: tuning out an over-trigger is a change to this file alone.

falsePositives.why: Ordinary sentences the list raises today. False positives are the accepted cost of a list that only ever raises, so these are reported by every platform's tests and never fail a build; they are here so that tuning one out is a visible, reviewable change rather than a guess.
